deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It holds three successive drafts of one programmatic sentence; the first two are partly crossed out or abandoned. The page continues the previous folio. There Riemann stated his principle: every action that depends on distance must be transmitted through the intervening medium. Elementary laws should therefore be partial differential equations linking the states of adjacent parts of a space-filling substance, not forces acting at a distance between discrete molecules. He then wrote Newtonian gravitation in field form. With potential V, density rho and gravitational force g = (g1,g2,g3) = grad V, he gave Poisson's equation Lap V = -rho, with V tending to 0 at infinity (rho is normalized so the 4*pi factor is absorbed). Equivalently, g1 dx1 + g2 dx2 + g3 dx3 is an exact differential (curl g = 0) and div g = -rho.

This page draws the physical interpretation:
(1) First draft: following the principle, to express the connection as simply as possible, gravity at each point must be regarded as a state, fixed by magnitude and direction, of a substance that fills space continuously.
(2) Second draft: 'Following the explanatory principles laid down, I now regard gravity as a state, determined at every point in magnitude and direction, of a substance continuously filling space, and assume that the states of the adjoining [parts] ...' (the sentence breaks off).
(3) Third fragment: '... so that ponderable masses act directly only on the state of the substance at the place where they are, and direct interaction occurs only between adjoining parts of the substance.'

In modern terms this proposes a vector field g(x) as a physical state of a medium (an ether). The local source law div g = -rho says matter affects the field only where it sits. The local compatibility condition curl g = 0 says field values at neighbouring points constrain each other. Together they are a local, contact-action (field-theoretic) reformulation of Newtonian gravity. No derivation is carried out on this page.
errors: No mathematical errors, because there is no mathematics on the page.
The drafts are incomplete: the second breaks off at 'der ineinander greifenden'.

results.what: Gravity interpreted as a vector-valued state (magnitude and direction) of a continuous space-filling medium. Masses act only locally on that state, and only adjacent parts of the medium interact directly (contact action replacing action at a distance).
results.modern_name: Field-theoretic (local) formulation of Newtonian gravity; ether / contact-action programme
results.usually_credited_to: Faraday, Maxwell, and Riemann himself in his natural-philosophy fragments (1850s)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material printed in Riemann's Werke (1876, Nachlass fragments 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' / 'Gravitation und Licht'). There he describes gravity as the state of a space-filling substance governed by local partial differential equations. The page contains only verbal drafts of this known idea.

checkable.asserts: If g = grad V then dg1/dx2 - dg2/dx1 = 0 (curl-free condition, previous page).

checkable.sympy: x1,x2,x3=symbols('x1 x2 x3'); V=Function('V')(x1,x2,x3); g=[diff(V,v) for v in (x1,x2,x3)]; simplify(sum(diff(g[i],v) for i,v in enumerate((x1,x2,x3))) - (diff(V,x1,2)+diff(V,x2,2)+diff(V,x3,2)))==0
checkable.asserts: div grad V = Laplacian V, so Lap V = -rho is equivalent to div g = -rho.
The potential of a point mass (1/r) is harmonic away from the source, consistent with the local field equations.

transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Nach den aufgestellten Princip muß man nun um den einfachsten Zusammenhang möglichst [...] auszudrücken die Schwerkraft als einen in jedem Punkte durch Größe und Richtung bestimmten Zustand eines den Raum stetig erfüllenden Stoffes'. 'jedem Punkte' is an interlinear insertion placed after 'als einen', not before 'ausgedrückt'.
'durch Größe und Richtung bestimmten' in the first draft appears as 'bestimmten'; the crossed-out word before 'eines' is probably 'Zustand' corrected, not a separate lost word.

'der ineinander greifenden' (second draft) and 'den ineinandergreifenden Stofftheilen' (third fragment) may instead read 'aneinander grenzenden' / 'aneinandergrenzenden'. This fits the previous page's wording 'Zustände an einander grenzender Stofftheile'. The handwriting is ambiguous.
Third fragment: 'und nur unmittelbare Wechselwirkung nur stattfindet' — the first 'nur' may be 'eine'.
In the second draft, 'nehme an, daß die Zustände der' has the 'der' at the line end struck through and repeated on the next line.
